question: Should OpenClaw bundle and own this Vault exec SecretRef resolver, or keep Vault on the external ClawHub/plugin path now that the manifest contract and claw-vault plugin exist?
rationale: The code can use the existing pluginIntegration seam, but bundling this resolver moves Vault credential handling, network access, dependency ownership, and operator policy mutation into core despite the repository's lean-core/ClawHub guardrail.

options.title: Keep Vault external
options.body: Close or pause the bundled-core path and direct users to the existing claw-vault plugin or a vetted ClawHub package while keeping OpenClaw core focused on the manifest contract.

options.title: Sponsor bundled Vault
options.body: Proceed only after the branch is made ready and mergeable, the multi-tenant docs are fixed, and maintainers/security approve the final resolver, dependency graph, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Narrow to core seam work
options.body: If a missing API is found, split that into a small core/plugin-SDK PR and leave the Vault implementation outside core.

recommendation.title: Keep Vault external
recommendation.body: Close or pause the bundled-core path and direct users to the existing claw-vault plugin or a vetted ClawHub package while keeping OpenClaw core focused on the manifest contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses security-sensitive CODEOWNERS surfaces and the core-versus-plugin product boundary, where his recent secrets hardening and repository-policy history are the strongest available routing signal.
